Preset.Comment: Smooth mode, no FX sets: transparent apart from the TickDelay latency.
The original's sound: Blocky mode, Smear on the mids, a little Contrast on top.
Blocky Clip across the spectrum: flattens loud partials into a buzzy, compressed tone.
Contrast +60%: strong partials get stronger, the noise between them recedes.
Contrast -60%: evens the spectrum out towards a breathy, noisy version of the input.
Weed +40%: removes weak bins, leaving the tonal skeleton. Good on noisy material.
Weed -40%: removes the strongest bins, leaving the residue and air.
Freeze holds the spectrum at load (or when Value rises from 0) and keeps sounding after the input stops. Re-trigger: set Value to 0, then back up.
Half frozen, half live: the held chord sits under whatever plays next.
Freezes only the low end (below 250 Hz) for a drone floor, the rest stays live.
2 s per-bin smoothing: transients dissolve into a slow-moving wash.
Blur and a little lift above 1 kHz: the top end trails and glows, the body stays tight.
Smooth-mode Smear plus a medium Blur: diffuse and reverb-like without a tail.
Spectral gate at -70 dBFS per bin: removes hiss and low-level hash between notes.
Hard gate on the highs only: just the loudest top partials get through, glittery and sparse.
-5 dB/oct above 200 Hz: warmer and duller without a filter's resonance.
+4 dB/oct above 1 kHz: adds air. Watch the level on bright sources.
Blocky mode, 1024-sample blocks, phase flattened: the classic robot buzz (pitch set by the hop).
Phase randomised over the voice range: pitched material turns into breath.
ShiftAdd of about +150 Hz (at 44.1 kHz) on the mids: inharmonic, bell-like doubling.
AutoHarm boosts the harmonic series of the loudest partial: richer, more focused tone.
Harmonic, odd series of 110 Hz cut by 12 dB: a hollow, clarinet-like colour on A-based material.
Connect a second machine to input 2 (Sidechain). Main takes on the sidechain's spectral shape: pad on Main, drums or voice on the sidechain.
50% cross-synthesis: Main keeps half its own character. Needs the sidechain connected.
PitchShift +12 semitones over the whole range. Smooth mode, Overlap 75%.
PitchShift -12 semitones; 8192-sample blocks keep bass notes clean.
Up a fifth (+7) mixed 50/50 with the dry signal (MixBack): instant parallel harmony.
+15 cents mixed with the dry signal: a chorus-like doubling without modulation.
Everything outside a two-octave band is removed, and the band sweeps up and down an octave every 32 ticks. LevelMatch off, so it gets quieter where the band finds little.
Two narrow notches sweeping in opposite directions (180 degrees apart): a phaser-like swirl.
PitchShift with its Value wobbling about a quarter-semitone every 1.5 ticks: vibrato in time with the song.
The spectral gate's threshold jumps between -10 and -70 dBFS every 2 ticks: rhythmic chopping.
An octave-wide Smear band that jumps to a random place every 2 ticks.
Two notches drifting at 0.15 and 0.1 Hz, free-running rather than locked to the song, so they never line up the same way twice: slow movement for pads.
The spectral gate's threshold jumps at 6 Hz whatever the tempo: a fast chop. Small blocks with Overlap 75% so the LFO can keep up.
PitchShift +12 with the set's Mix at 50%: the original plus an octave above, from one set (no MixBack needed).
PitchShift down a fifth (-7) at Mix 40%: a darker parallel voice under the original.
Heavy Smear at Mix 35%: adds breath and air while the original keeps its pitch and attack.
PitchShift +12 with Formant keep: an octave up without the chipmunk. Best on voices below about 200 Hz.
Up a fifth (+7) at Mix 50% with Formant keep: a harmony that sounds like the same singer.
No pitch change, formants up 4 semitones: a smaller, brighter voice at the same note.
A band-pass from G#3 to E4, set for C-4, that jumps to each note played in the Note column: the input sings the melody. LevelMatch off.
Harmonic boosts the harmonic series of the note played (FreqA follows, C-4 = as set): the input resonates in the key of the pattern.
PitchShift at Mix 50% with Formant keep; the Note column sets the interval (C-4 = unison, E-4 = a third up, G-3 = a fourth down).
